notes.front: What is Microsoft Entra ID?
notes.back: The Microsoft identity service whose dedicated, trusted instances, called tenants, hold an organisation’s directory of users and its registered apps.
notes.explanation: A tenant is set up either as a workforce tenant, for your employees and internal apps, or as an external tenant, for apps you publish to consumers and business customers.
notes.example: Like a company’s staff register and pass office rolled into one, with each organisation given its own locked branch of the service.
notes.source: Microsoft documentation (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub), “Microsoft Entra External ID Overview”, “What are workforce and external tenants?”
notes.evidence: A *tenant* is a dedicated and trusted instance of Microsoft Entra ID. It contains an organization's resources, including registered apps and a directory of users. There are two ways to configure a tenant, depending on how the organization intends to use the tenant and the resources that you want to manage:

notes.front: What is password hash synchronisation (PHS)?
notes.back: The simplest way to enable Microsoft Entra authentication for on-premises directory objects: users sign in with their on-premises username and password.
notes.explanation: The password hash is synchronised to Microsoft Entra ID, which validates the credentials itself in the cloud, so no other on-premises infrastructure is needed.
notes.example: Like giving a branch office a one-way fingerprint of each staff password so it can check sign-ins itself, without ever holding the passwords.
notes.source: Microsoft documentation (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub), “Authentication for Microsoft Entra hybrid identity solutions”, “Cloud authentication”
notes.evidence: The simplest way to enable authentication for on-premises directory objects in Microsoft Entra ID. Users can use the same username and password that they use on-premises without having to deploy any other infrastructure.

notes.front: What is pass-through authentication (PTA)?
notes.back: Cloud sign-in in which a software agent on on-premises servers validates users’ passwords directly against on-premises Active Directory.
notes.explanation: The password validation therefore doesn’t happen in the cloud.
notes.example: Like a hotel that rings your employer to confirm your staff card every time you check in, instead of keeping its own copy of the card.
notes.source: Microsoft documentation (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub), “Authentication for Microsoft Entra hybrid identity solutions”, “Cloud authentication”
notes.evidence: Provides a simple password validation for Microsoft Entra authentication services by using a software agent that runs on one or more on-premises servers. The servers validate the users directly with your on-premises Active Directory, which ensures that the password validation doesn't happen in the cloud.

notes.front: What is federated authentication for a Microsoft Entra hybrid identity solution?
notes.back: Microsoft Entra ID hands authentication to a separate trusted system, such as on-premises Active Directory Federation Services, to validate the password.
notes.explanation: That separate system can add its own requirements, such as third-party multifactor authentication.
notes.example: Like a members’ club that admits anyone vouched for by a partner club’s doorman, instead of checking them itself.
notes.source: Microsoft documentation (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub), “Authentication for Microsoft Entra hybrid identity solutions”, “Federated authentication”
notes.evidence: When you choose this authentication method, Microsoft Entra ID hands off the authentication process to a separate trusted authentication system, such as on-premises Active Directory Federation Services (AD FS), to validate the user's password. The authentication system can provide other advanced authentication requirements, for example, third-party multifactor authentication.

notes.front: What does seamless single sign-on (Seamless SSO) do?
notes.back: It eliminates unnecessary sign-in prompts for users who are already signed in.
notes.explanation: Microsoft recommends it, together with PHS, when Windows devices can’t be joined to Microsoft Entra ID.
notes.example: Like a staff badge that opens every internal door once you have badged in at the front entrance.
notes.source: Microsoft documentation (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub), “Authentication for Microsoft Entra hybrid identity solutions”, “Cloud authentication: Password hash synchronization”
notes.evidence: If you can't join your Windows devices to Microsoft Entra ID, we recommend deploying seamless SSO with password hash synchronization. Seamless SSO eliminates unnecessary prompts when users are signed in.

notes.front: What is Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync?
notes.back: A hybrid identity service giving cloud-managed synchronisation of users, groups and contacts between Active Directory and Microsoft Entra ID.
notes.explanation: It is Microsoft’s strategic direction for hybrid identity, using lightweight agents to simplify deployment and management.
notes.example: Like a courier network run from head office that sends small vans to each branch, instead of every branch running its own post room.
notes.source: Microsoft documentation (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub), “What is Microsoft Entra Cloud sync?”, “What is Microsoft Entra Cloud sync?”
notes.evidence: Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync is a hybrid identity synchronization service that provides modern, cloud-managed synchronization of users, groups, and contacts between Active Directory and Microsoft Entra ID. It represents Microsoft's strategic direction for hybrid identity, offering a lightweight, agent-based approach that simplifies deployment and management

notes.front: What is Microsoft Entra multifactor authentication (MFA)?
notes.back: A process that prompts users during sign-in for an additional form of identification, such as a code on their phone or a fingerprint scan.
notes.explanation: Relying on a password alone leaves an insecure vector for attack.
notes.example: Like a bank card that needs both the card and its secret number before the cash machine pays out, but for signing in.
notes.source: Microsoft documentation (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub), “Microsoft Entra multifactor authentication overview”, “How it works: Microsoft Entra multifactor authentication”
notes.evidence: Multifactor authentication is a process in which users are prompted during the sign-in process for an additional form of identification, such as a code on their cellphone or a fingerprint scan. If you only use a password to authenticate a user, it leaves an insecure vector for attack.

notes.front: What is Microsoft Entra Conditional Access?
notes.back: Microsoft’s Zero Trust policy engine: it brings signals together to make access decisions and enforce organisational policies.
notes.explanation: It takes signals from various sources into account when it enforces a policy decision.
notes.example: Like a doorman who checks who you are, the time and where you have come from before deciding to admit you, refuse you or ask for more proof.
notes.source: Microsoft documentation (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub), “Microsoft Entra Conditional Access: Zero Trust Policy Engine”, “Overview”
notes.evidence: Microsoft Entra Conditional Access brings signals together, to make decisions, and enforce organizational policies. Conditional Access is Microsoft's Zero Trust policy engine taking signals from various sources into account when enforcing policy decisions.

notes.front: What is Microsoft Entra ID Protection?
notes.back: A service that helps organisations detect, investigate and remediate identity-based risks.
notes.explanation: Its risk findings can feed tools such as Conditional Access to make access decisions, or go to a security information and event management tool.
notes.example: Like a bank’s fraud team that flags a card used in two countries within an hour, but for accounts and sign-ins.
notes.source: Microsoft documentation (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub), “What is Microsoft Entra ID Protection?”, “What is Microsoft Entra ID Protection?”
notes.evidence: Microsoft Entra ID Protection helps organizations detect, investigate, and remediate identity-based risks. These risks can be fed into tools like Conditional Access to make access decisions or sent to a security information and event management (SIEM) tool for further investigation and correlation.

notes.front: What is Microsoft Entra External ID?
notes.back: Microsoft Entra solutions that let people outside your organisation, such as partners, consumers and business customers, securely access your apps and resources.
notes.explanation: Those external users can bring their own identities rather than being issued new ones.
notes.example: Like a venue that lets guests in on their own passports or club cards instead of printing everyone a new badge.
notes.source: Microsoft documentation (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub), “Microsoft Entra External ID Overview”, “Introduction to Microsoft Entra External ID”
notes.evidence: Microsoft Entra External ID combines powerful solutions for working with people outside your organization. With External ID capabilities, you can allow external identities to securely access your apps and resources. Whether you're working with external partners, consumers, or business customers, users can bring their own identities.

notes.front: What is B2B collaboration in Microsoft Entra External ID?
notes.back: A way for your workforce to collaborate with external business partners, who sign in with their own credentials to apps and resources you share.
notes.explanation: You invite the partners in and decide which apps and resources to share with them.
notes.example: Like issuing visitor passes to a supplier’s staff, who still prove who they are with their own company ID.
notes.source: Microsoft documentation (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub), “Microsoft Entra External ID Overview”, “Collaborate with business guests”
notes.evidence: External ID B2B collaboration allows your workforce to collaborate with external business partners. You can invite anyone to sign in to your Microsoft Entra organization by using their own credentials so they can access the apps and resources that you want to share with them.

notes.front: What is B2B direct connect?
notes.back: A two-way trust with another Microsoft Entra organisation that enables the Teams Connect shared channels feature.
notes.explanation: Users can then sign in to shared channels for chat, calls, file sharing and app sharing.
notes.example: Like two neighbouring schools running a joint class, where each pupil keeps using their own school’s pass.
notes.source: Microsoft documentation (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub), “Microsoft Entra External ID Overview”, “B2B direct connect”
notes.evidence: You can use B2B direct connect to create two-way trust relationships with other Microsoft Entra organizations to enable the Teams Connect shared channels feature. This feature allows users to seamlessly sign in to Teams shared channels for chat, calls, file sharing, and app sharing.

notes.front: What is Azure Active Directory B2C (Azure AD B2C)?
notes.back: A legacy solution for customer identity and access management, with its own separate consumer-based directory.
notes.explanation: Each Azure AD B2C tenant is separate and distinct from Microsoft Entra ID tenants.
notes.example: Like an old stand-alone loyalty-card database kept apart from a shop’s staff records.
notes.source: Microsoft documentation (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub), “Microsoft Entra External ID Overview”, “Azure Active Directory B2C (Azure AD B2C)”
notes.evidence: Azure AD B2C is a legacy solution for customer identity and access management. Azure AD B2C includes a separate consumer-based directory that you manage in the Azure portal through the Azure AD B2C service. Each Azure AD B2C tenant is separate and distinct from other Microsoft Entra ID and Azure AD B2C tenants.

notes.front: What are managed identities for Azure resources?
notes.back: Identities that let applications obtain Microsoft Entra tokens without anyone having to manage credentials.
notes.explanation: Handling secrets and certificates by hand is a known source of security issues and outages.
notes.example: Like a staff lanyard that the building issues and renews by itself, so nobody has to carry or copy a key.
notes.source: Microsoft documentation (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub), “Managed identities for Azure resources”, “What is managed identities for Azure resources?”
notes.evidence: Manual handling of secrets and certificates are a known source of security issues and outages. Managed identities eliminate the need for developers to manage these credentials. Applications can use managed identities to obtain Microsoft Entra tokens without having to manage any credentials.

notes.front: What is Microsoft Entra Domain Services?
notes.back: Managed domain services, such as domain join, Group Policy and Kerberos authentication, without deploying, managing or patching domain controllers.
notes.explanation: Microsoft runs the domain controllers, so you use the services without looking after the servers yourself.
notes.example: Like renting a fully staffed post room for your old paper-based systems instead of hiring and training your own clerks.
notes.source: Microsoft documentation (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub), “Overview of Microsoft Entra Domain Services”, “What is Microsoft Entra Domain Services?”
notes.evidence: Microsoft Entra Domain Services provides managed domain services such as domain join, group policy, lightweight directory access protocol (LDAP), and Kerberos/NTLM authentication. You use these domain services without the need to deploy, manage, and patch domain controllers (DCs) in the cloud.

notes.front: With cloud authentication for a hybrid identity solution, what are the two options?
notes.back: Password hash synchronisation and pass-through authentication.
notes.explanation: In cloud authentication, Microsoft Entra ID itself handles users’ sign-in.
notes.source: Microsoft documentation (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub), “Authentication for Microsoft Entra hybrid identity solutions”, “Cloud authentication”
notes.evidence: When you choose this authentication method, Microsoft Entra ID handles users' sign-in process. Coupled with single sign-on (SSO), users can sign in to cloud apps without having to reenter their credentials. With cloud authentication, you can choose from two options:

notes.front: Which tool configures the chosen hybrid authentication method and also provisions users in the cloud?
notes.back: Microsoft Entra Connect.
notes.explanation: Choosing the method is a crucial first decision in setting up a hybrid identity solution.
notes.source: Microsoft documentation (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub), “Authentication for Microsoft Entra hybrid identity solutions”, “Authentication methods”
notes.evidence: Choosing the correct authentication method is a crucial first decision in setting up a Microsoft Entra hybrid identity solution. The authentication method you choose, is configured by using Microsoft Entra Connect, which also provisions users in the cloud.

notes.front: How often does PHS run as part of Microsoft Entra Connect Sync?
notes.back: Every two minutes.
notes.explanation: It needs the least deployment, maintenance and infrastructure effort of the methods.
notes.source: Microsoft documentation (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub), “Authentication for Microsoft Entra hybrid identity solutions”, “Cloud authentication: Password hash synchronization”
notes.evidence: Password hash synchronization requires the least effort regarding deployment, maintenance, and infrastructure. This level of effort typically applies to organizations that only need their users to sign in to Microsoft 365, SaaS apps, and other Microsoft Entra ID-based resources. When turned on, password hash synchronization is part of the Microsoft Entra Connect Sync process and runs every two minutes.

notes.front: What are two premium features of Microsoft Entra ID that require PHS whichever authentication method you choose?
notes.back: Microsoft Entra ID Protection and Microsoft Entra Domain Services.
notes.explanation: The requirement stands even if users sign in through pass-through authentication or federation.
notes.source: Microsoft documentation (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub), “Authentication for Microsoft Entra hybrid identity solutions”, “Cloud authentication”
notes.evidence: Some premium features of Microsoft Entra ID, like Microsoft Entra ID Protection and Microsoft Entra Domain Services, require password hash synchronization, no matter which authentication method you choose.

notes.front: Which ID Protection report depends on PHS, whatever sign-in method you use?
notes.back: The Users with leaked credentials report.
notes.explanation: PHS configured in advance also lets an organisation fail over to it if the primary sign-in method fails.
notes.source: Microsoft documentation (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub), “Authentication for Microsoft Entra hybrid identity solutions”, “Decision tree”
notes.evidence: Microsoft Entra ID Protection requires Password Hash Sync regardless of which sign-in method you choose, to provide the *Users with leaked credentials* report. Organizations can fail over to Password Hash Sync if their primary sign-in method fails and it was configured before the failure event.

notes.front: How many PTA agents does Microsoft recommend in total?
notes.back: Three: the first on the Microsoft Entra Connect server plus two extra agents.
notes.explanation: With three agents, one can still fail while another is down for maintenance.
notes.source: Microsoft documentation (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub), “Authentication for Microsoft Entra hybrid identity solutions”, “Cloud authentication: Pass-through Authentication”
notes.evidence: We recommend that you deploy two extra pass-through authentication agents. These extras are in addition to the first agent on the Microsoft Entra Connect server. This other deployment ensures high availability of authentication requests. When you have three agents deployed, one agent can still fail when another agent is down for maintenance.

notes.front: Which on-premises account rules does PTA enforce at the moment of sign-in?
notes.back: Account states such as disabled or locked out, password expiry, and the hours a user may sign in.
notes.explanation: Access is denied at sign-in if the on-premises account policy says no.
notes.source: Microsoft documentation (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub), “Authentication for Microsoft Entra hybrid identity solutions”, “Cloud authentication: Pass-through Authentication”
notes.evidence: Pass-through Authentication enforces the on-premises account policy at the time of sign-in. For example, access is denied when an on-premises user's account state is disabled, locked out, or their password expires or the logon attempt falls outside the hours when the user is allowed to sign in.

notes.front: If PTA agents can’t validate credentials because of a major on-premises failure, does sign-in fail over to PHS automatically?
notes.back: No; you must switch the sign-on method manually in Microsoft Entra Connect.
notes.explanation: PHS can act as the backup method, but only after someone switches to it.
notes.source: Microsoft documentation (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub), “Authentication for Microsoft Entra hybrid identity solutions”, “Cloud authentication: Pass-through Authentication”
notes.evidence: You can use password hash synchronization as a backup authentication method for pass-through authentication, when the agents can't validate a user's credentials due to a significant on-premises failure. Fail over to password hash synchronization doesn't happen automatically and you must use Microsoft Entra Connect to switch the sign-on method manually.

notes.front: What are two common requirements that make a federated authentication solution necessary?
notes.back: Third-party multifactor providers that need a federated identity provider, and authentication through third-party authentication solutions.
notes.explanation: Federation is required when there is an authentication requirement that Microsoft Entra ID doesn’t support natively.
notes.source: Microsoft documentation (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub), “Authentication for Microsoft Entra hybrid identity solutions”, “Federated authentication”
notes.evidence: A federated authentication solution is required when customers have an authentication requirement that Microsoft Entra ID doesn't support natively. See detailed information to help you choose the right sign-in option. Consider the following common requirements: * Third-party multifactor providers requiring a federated identity provider. * Authentication by using third-party authentication solutions.

notes.front: When ransomware took on-premises servers down, how did organisations that already had PHS enabled recover sign-in?
notes.back: They switched their primary authentication method to PHS and were back online within hours.
notes.explanation: This is one reason Microsoft recommends enabling PHS alongside federation or pass-through authentication.
notes.source: Microsoft documentation (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub), “Authentication for Microsoft Entra hybrid identity solutions”, “Recommendations”
notes.evidence: Organizations that previously also turned on password hash synchronization on top of federated or pass-through authentication changed their primary authentication method to then use password hash synchronization. They were back online in a matter of hours.

notes.front: In Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync, what does the Microsoft Entra provisioning agent do?
notes.back: It runs on-premises as a lightweight, secure bridge between Active Directory and Microsoft Entra ID.
notes.explanation: It needs only outbound connections and receives automatic updates from the cloud.
notes.source: Microsoft documentation (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub), “What is Microsoft Entra Cloud sync?”, “Core architecture and components”
notes.evidence: **Microsoft Entra provisioning agent**: A lightweight, on-premises agent that acts as a secure bridge between Active Directory and Microsoft Entra ID. The agent uses the same proven technology as Microsoft Entra Application Proxy and Pass-Through Authentication, requiring only outbound connections and providing automatic updates from the cloud.

notes.front: Microsoft Entra MFA requires two or more of which three kinds of authentication method?
notes.back: Something you know, something you have, and something you are.
notes.explanation: Typical examples are a password, a trusted phone or hardware key, and a fingerprint or face scan.
notes.source: Microsoft documentation (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub), “Microsoft Entra multifactor authentication overview”, “How it works: Microsoft Entra multifactor authentication”
notes.evidence: Microsoft Entra multifactor authentication works by requiring two or more of the following authentication methods: * Something you know, typically a password. * Something you have, such as a trusted device that's not easily duplicated, like a phone or hardware key. * Something you are - biometrics like a fingerprint or face scan.

notes.front: Do apps and services need changing to use Microsoft Entra MFA?
notes.back: No.
notes.explanation: The verification prompts are part of the Microsoft Entra sign-in, which requests and processes the challenge when needed.
notes.source: Microsoft documentation (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub), “Microsoft Entra multifactor authentication overview”, “How it works: Microsoft Entra multifactor authentication”
notes.evidence: You don't need to change apps and services to use Microsoft Entra multifactor authentication. The verification prompts are part of the Microsoft Entra sign-in, which automatically requests and processes the MFA challenge when needed.

notes.front: Apart from a text message or a voice call, what are two verification methods users can register for Microsoft Entra MFA?
notes.back: For example, Microsoft Authenticator and Windows Hello for Business.
notes.explanation: The list is open: passkeys are among the other options.
notes.source: Microsoft documentation (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub), “Microsoft Entra multifactor authentication overview”, “Available verification methods”
notes.evidence: The following additional forms of verification can be used with Microsoft Entra multifactor authentication: * Microsoft Authenticator * Authenticator Lite (in Outlook) * Windows Hello for Business * Passkey (FIDO2)

notes.front: At what point in sign-in are Conditional Access policies enforced?
notes.back: After first-factor authentication is completed.
notes.explanation: Conditional Access isn’t intended as the frontline defence against attacks such as denial of service, though it can use their signals.
notes.source: Microsoft documentation (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub), “Microsoft Entra Conditional Access: Zero Trust Policy Engine”, “Overview”
notes.evidence: Conditional Access policies are enforced after first-factor authentication is completed. Conditional Access isn't intended to be an organization's frontline defense for scenarios like denial-of-service (DoS) attacks, but it can use signals from these events to determine access.

notes.front: Which Conditional Access signal lets policies target specific users, groups and agents?
notes.back: User, group or agent.
notes.explanation: Targeting identities gives admins fine-grained control over access.
notes.source: Microsoft documentation (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub), “Microsoft Entra Conditional Access: Zero Trust Policy Engine”, “Common signals”
notes.evidence: Policies can be targeted to specific users, groups, and agents (Preview) giving admins fine-grained control over access.

notes.front: Which Conditional Access signal lets admins block or allow traffic from entire countries or regions?
notes.back: Location information (address ranges).
notes.explanation: Organisations can also define their own address ranges for use in policy decisions.
notes.source: Microsoft documentation (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub), “Microsoft Entra Conditional Access: Zero Trust Policy Engine”, “Common signals”
notes.evidence: Organizations can create IP address ranges that can be used when making policy decisions. - Admins can specify entire countries/regions IP ranges to block or allow traffic from.

notes.front: Which Conditional Access signal can target policies at specific machines, such as privileged access workstations?
notes.back: Device, using filters for devices.
notes.explanation: Device platform or a device’s marked state can also be used when enforcing policies.
notes.source: Microsoft documentation (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub), “Microsoft Entra Conditional Access: Zero Trust Policy Engine”, “Common signals”
notes.evidence: Users with devices of specific platforms or marked with a specific state can be used when enforcing Conditional Access policies. - Use filters for devices to target policies to specific devices like privileged access workstations.

notes.front: Which Conditional Access signal triggers different policies when users try to reach particular apps?
notes.back: Application.
notes.explanation: Policies can apply to cloud apps, on-premises applications and agent resources.
notes.source: Microsoft documentation (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub), “Microsoft Entra Conditional Access: Zero Trust Policy Engine”, “Common signals”
notes.evidence: Trigger different Conditional Access policies when users attempt to access specific applications. - Apply policies to traditional cloud apps, on-premises applications, and agent resources.

notes.front: Which Conditional Access signal brings in ID Protection’s findings about risky users and sign-in behaviour?
notes.back: Real-time and calculated risk detection.
notes.explanation: It integrates ID Protection signals to identify and remediate risk.
notes.source: Microsoft documentation (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub), “Microsoft Entra Conditional Access: Zero Trust Policy Engine”, “Common signals”
notes.evidence: Integrates signals from Microsoft Entra ID Protection to identify and remediate risky users, sign-in behavior, and agent activities.

notes.front: Which Conditional Access signal source monitors and controls user access to applications and sessions in real time?
notes.back: Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps.
notes.explanation: The integration improves visibility and control over access and activity in the cloud environment.
notes.source: Microsoft documentation (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub), “Microsoft Entra Conditional Access: Zero Trust Policy Engine”, “Common signals”
notes.evidence: Monitors and controls user application access and sessions in real time. This integration improves visibility and control over access and activities in your cloud environment.

notes.front: What is the most restrictive Conditional Access decision?
notes.back: Block access.
notes.explanation: Grant access is the less restrictive decision, and it may still require further controls.
notes.source: Microsoft documentation (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub), “Microsoft Entra Conditional Access: Zero Trust Policy Engine”, “Common decisions”
notes.evidence: Block access is the most restrictive decision. - Grant access - A less restrictive decision that might require one or more of the following options:

notes.front: What are two controls that a Conditional Access grant decision can require?
notes.back: For example, multifactor authentication and a device marked as compliant.
notes.explanation: Others include an approved client app, a password change and accepting terms of use.
notes.source: Microsoft documentation (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub), “Microsoft Entra Conditional Access: Zero Trust Policy Engine”, “Common decisions”
notes.evidence: - Require multifactor authentication - Require authentication strength - Require the device to be marked as compliant - Require a Microsoft Entra hybrid joined device - Require an approved client app - Require an app protection policy - Require a password change - Require terms of use

notes.front: What happens to Conditional Access policies when the licences they need expire?
notes.back: They aren’t disabled or deleted automatically; you can view and delete them but not update them.
notes.explanation: This graceful state lets customers move away from the policies without a sudden change in security posture.
notes.source: Microsoft documentation (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub), “Microsoft Entra Conditional Access: Zero Trust Policy Engine”, “License requirements”
notes.evidence: When the licenses required for Conditional Access expire, policies aren't automatically disabled or deleted. This graceful state lets customers migrate away from Conditional Access policies without a sudden change in their security posture. You can view and delete remaining policies, but you can't update them.

notes.front: What do risk-based Conditional Access policies, based on sign-in risk and user risk, require?
notes.back: Microsoft Entra ID Protection.
notes.explanation: ID Protection is itself a premium feature with its own licence requirement.
notes.source: Microsoft documentation (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub), “Microsoft Entra Conditional Access: Zero Trust Policy Engine”, “License requirements”
notes.evidence: Risk-based Conditional Access policies (sign-in risk and user risk) require Microsoft Entra ID Protection, which is a Microsoft Entra ID P2 feature.

notes.front: What are the three key reports ID Protection gives administrators for investigating risk?
notes.back: Risk detections, risky sign-ins and risky users.
notes.explanation: Any risk detected on an identity is tracked through this reporting.
notes.source: Microsoft documentation (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub), “What is Microsoft Entra ID Protection?”, “Investigate”
notes.evidence: Any risks detected on an identity are tracked with reporting. ID Protection provides three key reports for administrators to investigate risks and take action: - **Risk detections:** Each risk detected is reported as a risk detection.

notes.front: Can an organisation on the free edition of Microsoft Entra ID use ID Protection’s sign-in and user risk policies?
notes.back: No; risk policies come only with the highest premium edition or Microsoft Entra Suite.
notes.explanation: Neither the free edition nor the first premium edition includes them.
notes.source: Microsoft documentation (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub), “What is Microsoft Entra ID Protection?”, “License requirements”
notes.evidence:
| Risk policies | Sign-in and user risk policies (via ID Protection or Conditional Access)
Includes Microsoft managed remediation policies | No | No | Yes |

notes.front: Where is the user object for a B2B collaboration guest created?
notes.back: In the same directory as your employees.
notes.explanation: You can manage it like any other user object, for example by adding it to groups.
notes.source: Microsoft documentation (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub), “Microsoft Entra External ID Overview”, “Collaborate with business guests”
notes.evidence: A user object is created for business guests in the same directory that you use for your employees. You can manage this user object like other user objects in your directory. For example, you can add it to groups.

notes.front: Does your organisation hold credentials for its B2B collaboration guests?
notes.back: No; guests authenticate with their home organisation or identity provider.
notes.explanation: Your organisation then checks whether they are eligible for guest collaboration.
notes.source: Microsoft documentation (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub), “Microsoft Entra External ID Overview”, “Collaborate with business guests”
notes.evidence: There are no credentials associated with business guests. Instead, they authenticate with their home organization or identity provider, and then your organization checks their eligibility for guest collaboration.

notes.front: Can users in an external tenant get single sign-on to Microsoft 365?
notes.back: No; single sign-on is supported only to apps registered in the external tenant.
notes.explanation: A workforce tenant, by contrast, supports single sign-on to all Microsoft Entra-connected apps.
notes.source: Microsoft documentation (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub), “Microsoft Entra External ID Overview”, “Comparing External ID feature sets”
notes.evidence: | Single sign-on (SSO) | SSO to all Microsoft Entra-connected apps is supported. For example, you can provide access to Microsoft 365 or on-premises apps, and to other SaaS apps such as Salesforce or Workday. | SSO to apps registered in the external tenant is supported. SSO to Microsoft 365 or to other Microsoft SaaS apps isn't supported. |

notes.front: Which type of managed identity is recommended for Microsoft services?
notes.back: User-assigned.
notes.explanation: User-assigned identities are provisioned independently of compute and can be assigned to several compute resources.
notes.source: Microsoft documentation (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub), “Managed identities for Azure resources”, “Managed identity types”
notes.evidence: User-assigned managed identities, which are provisioned independently from compute and can be assigned to multiple compute resources, are the recommended managed identity type for Microsoft services.

notes.front: When an Azure resource with a system-assigned managed identity is deleted, Azure {{c1::automatically deletes its service principal}}.
notes.back: automatically deletes its service principal
notes.explanation: The service principal of a system-assigned identity is tied to the lifecycle of its resource.
notes.source: Microsoft documentation (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub), “Managed identities for Azure resources”, “Managed identity types”
notes.evidence: The service principal is tied to the lifecycle of that Azure resource. When the Azure resource is deleted, Azure automatically deletes the service principal for you.

notes.front: Which resource can use a system-assigned managed identity to request tokens from Microsoft Entra ID?
notes.back: Only the Azure resource it was enabled on.
notes.explanation: By design the identity belongs to that one resource, not shared with any other.
notes.source: Microsoft documentation (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub), “Managed identities for Azure resources”, “Managed identity types”
notes.evidence: By design, only that Azure resource can use this identity to request tokens from Microsoft Entra ID.

notes.front: How many managed identities can be used as federated identity credentials on one Microsoft Entra ID application?
notes.back: Up to 20.
notes.explanation: Using a managed identity this way is the recommended credential-free approach whenever a Microsoft Entra ID app is needed.
notes.source: Microsoft documentation (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub), “Managed identities for Azure resources”, “Use managed identity as a Federated Identity Credential (FIC) on an Entra ID app”
notes.evidence: Workload Identity Federation enables using a managed identity as a credential, just like certificate or password, on Entra ID Applications. Whenever an Entra ID app is required, this is the recommended way to be credential-free. There's a limit of 20 FICs when using managed identities as FIC on an Entra ID App.

notes.front: When you create a Domain Services managed domain, what domain controllers are deployed?
notes.back: Two Windows Server domain controllers, as a replica set in your chosen Azure region, fully managed by Microsoft.
notes.explanation: You don’t need to configure, patch or monitor them.
notes.source: Microsoft documentation (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub), “Overview of Microsoft Entra Domain Services”, “How does Microsoft Entra Domain Services work?”
notes.evidence: Two Windows Server domain controllers are deployed into your selected Azure region as part of a replica set. These domain controllers are fully managed by Microsoft. You don’t need to configure, patch, or monitor them.

notes.front: In which direction does a Domain Services managed domain synchronise with Microsoft Entra ID?
notes.back: One way, from Microsoft Entra ID into the managed domain.
notes.explanation: Users, groups and credentials from Microsoft Entra ID are made available in the managed domain for Azure apps and virtual machines.
notes.source: Microsoft documentation (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub), “Overview of Microsoft Entra Domain Services”, “How does Microsoft Entra Domain Services work?”
notes.evidence: A managed domain is configured to perform a one‑way synchronization from Microsoft Entra ID. Users, groups, and credentials from Microsoft Entra ID are made available in the managed domain so that applications, services, and virtual machines in Azure can use familiar AD DS capabilities

notes.front: Is a Domain Services managed domain an extension of your on-premises domain?
notes.back: No; it is a stand-alone domain.
notes.explanation: If hybrid access is needed, forest trusts with on-premises environments can be configured.
notes.source: Microsoft documentation (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub), “Overview of Microsoft Entra Domain Services”, “Microsoft Entra Domain Services features and benefits”
notes.evidence: A managed domain is a stand‑alone domain and isn’t an extension of an on‑premises domain. If required, you can [configure forest trusts][forest-trusts] with on‑premises AD DS environments to support hybrid access scenario.

notes.front: Is Domain Services meant as a general replacement for on-premises Active Directory?
notes.back: No; it is a transitional capability for Azure-hosted workloads that need legacy authentication.
notes.explanation: Nor is it a substitute for cloud-native identity services.
notes.source: Microsoft documentation (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub), “Overview of Microsoft Entra Domain Services”, “When to use Microsoft Entra Domain Services”
notes.evidence: You can use Domain Services as a transitional capability for Azure-hosted workloads that require legacy authentication, rather than as a general replacement for your on-premises Active Directory or a substitute for cloud-native identity services.

notes.front: A building society must enforce on-premises account lockouts, password policies and permitted sign-in hours immediately at every cloud sign-in. It has no federation servers and wants little extra infrastructure. Which method fits?
notes.back: Pass-through authentication.
notes.choices:
A) Password hash synchronisation alone
B) Pass-through authentication
C) Federation with new Active Directory Federation Services servers
notes.choicesExplained: A: PHS doesn’t immediately enforce changes in on-premises account states. C: federation needs a much larger on-premises footprint, which the society wants to avoid.
notes.explanation: PTA is the cloud method for organisations that must enforce on-premises account states, password policies and sign-in hours immediately.
notes.source: Microsoft documentation (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub), “Authentication for Microsoft Entra hybrid identity solutions”, “Cloud authentication”
notes.evidence: Companies with a security requirement to immediately enforce on-premises user account states, password policies, and sign-in hours might use this authentication method.

notes.front: A 40-person firm with an on-premises directory only needs staff to sign in to Microsoft 365 and other cloud apps, and wants the least deployment and maintenance effort. Which method fits?
notes.back: Password hash synchronisation.
notes.choices:
A) Password hash synchronisation
B) Pass-through authentication
C) Federated authentication
notes.choicesExplained: B: PTA needs agents installed on on-premises servers. C: federation relies on an external system that the firm would have to deploy and run.
notes.explanation: PHS needs the least effort in deployment, maintenance and infrastructure, which typically suits organisations whose users only sign in to Microsoft 365 and similar cloud resources.
notes.source: Microsoft documentation (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub), “Authentication for Microsoft Entra hybrid identity solutions”, “Cloud authentication: Password hash synchronization”
notes.evidence: Password hash synchronization requires the least effort regarding deployment, maintenance, and infrastructure. This level of effort typically applies to organizations that only need their users to sign in to Microsoft 365, SaaS apps, and other Microsoft Entra ID-based resources.

notes.front: An organisation’s users must keep signing in with the sAMAccountName form rather than a user principal name, and its third-party multifactor provider needs a federated identity provider. Which method fits?
notes.back: Federated authentication.
notes.choices:
A) Password hash synchronisation
B) Pass-through authentication
C) Federated authentication
notes.choicesExplained: A and B: both cloud methods support user principal name sign-in, not the sAMAccountName form, and neither works with a provider that needs a federated identity provider.
notes.explanation: Federation is required when an authentication requirement isn’t supported natively by Microsoft Entra ID, and both of these are listed examples.
notes.source: Microsoft documentation (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub), “Authentication for Microsoft Entra hybrid identity solutions”, “Federated authentication”
notes.evidence: * Third-party multifactor providers requiring a federated identity provider. * Authentication by using third-party authentication solutions. See the Microsoft Entra federation compatibility list. * Sign in that requires a sAMAccountName, for example DOMAIN\username, instead of a User Principal Name (UPN), for example, user@domain.com.

notes.front: After an acquisition, a company must synchronise users from two Active Directory forests that can’t be connected into its single Microsoft Entra tenant, without consolidating the forests. What fits best?
notes.back: Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync.
notes.choices:
A) Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync
B) Merge the forests first, then synchronise
C) Create a second Microsoft Entra tenant for the acquired company
notes.choicesExplained: B: forest consolidation is exactly what the company wants to avoid, and Cloud Sync makes it unnecessary. C: a second tenant splits identities instead of bringing them into one tenant.
notes.explanation: Cloud Sync’s architecture enables synchronising disconnected forests into one tenant, which is complex or impossible with traditional approaches.
notes.source: Microsoft documentation (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub), “What is Microsoft Entra Cloud sync?”, “How is Microsoft Entra Cloud sync different from Microsoft Entra Connect sync?”
notes.evidence: This architectural difference enables scenarios that are complex or impossible with traditional approaches, such as synchronizing from multiple disconnected forests to a single Microsoft Entra tenant without forest consolidation.

notes.front: Staff should sign in normally in the office on registered devices, but be asked for MFA when working remotely or on a personal device. What should you configure?
notes.back: A Conditional Access policy that requires MFA in those conditions.
notes.choices:
A) A Conditional Access policy that requires MFA in those conditions
B) Security defaults for all users
C) PHS
notes.choicesExplained: B: security defaults quickly turn on Microsoft Authenticator for everyone, without this conditional control. C: PHS is a sign-in method, not a rule for when to prompt for MFA.
notes.explanation: Conditional Access gives the more granular control to decide the events or applications that need MFA.
notes.source: Microsoft documentation (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub), “Microsoft Entra multifactor authentication overview”, “How to enable and use Microsoft Entra multifactor authentication”
notes.evidence: For more granular controls, you can use Conditional Access policies to define events or applications that require MFA. These policies can allow regular sign-in when the user is on the corporate network or a registered device but prompt for additional verification factors when the user is remote or on a personal device.

notes.front: A company never does business in a certain country and wants to stop all sign-ins from there. How should Conditional Access handle it?
notes.back: Use the location signal for that country with a block access decision.
notes.choices:
A) Location signal with a block access decision
B) Location signal with a grant decision requiring MFA
C) Device signal with a block access decision
notes.choicesExplained: B: granting with MFA still lets those sign-ins through. C: the device signal targets device platforms or states, not where traffic comes from.
notes.explanation: Admins can specify whole countries or regions to block or allow, and block is the most restrictive decision.
notes.source: Microsoft documentation (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub), “Microsoft Entra Conditional Access: Zero Trust Policy Engine”, “Common signals”
notes.evidence: Admins can specify entire countries/regions IP ranges to block or allow traffic from.

notes.front: The finance app may be used only from company-managed devices that meet the compliance policy. Which Conditional Access decision fits?
notes.back: Grant access, requiring the device to be marked as compliant.
notes.choices:
A) Grant access, requiring a compliant device
B) Block access for everyone
C) Grant access, requiring a password change
notes.choicesExplained: B: blocking would stop compliant devices too. C: a password change says nothing about the device being used.
notes.explanation: Grant is the less restrictive decision that can require controls, and a compliant device is one of them.
notes.source: Microsoft documentation (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub), “Microsoft Entra Conditional Access: Zero Trust Policy Engine”, “Common decisions”
notes.evidence: - Grant access - A less restrictive decision that might require one or more of the following options: - Require multifactor authentication - Require authentication strength - Require the device to be marked as compliant

notes.front: Security wants any user rated high risk to be made to do a secure password reset at next sign-in, without an admin stepping in. What should be set up?
notes.back: A risk-based Conditional Access policy, using ID Protection’s risk level, that requires a secure password reset.
notes.choices:
A) A risk-based Conditional Access policy requiring a secure password reset
B) A weekly manual review of the Risky users report
C) An MFA registration campaign
notes.choicesExplained: B: manual review is what happens when automatic remediation isn’t enabled. C: registering for MFA doesn’t act on a detected risk.
notes.explanation: If the user completes the required control, the risk is remediated automatically.
notes.source: Microsoft documentation (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub), “What is Microsoft Entra ID Protection?”, “Automatic remediation”
notes.evidence: Risk-based Conditional Access policies can be enabled to require access controls such as providing a strong authentication method, perform multifactor authentication, or perform a secure password reset based on the detected risk level. If the user successfully completes the access control, the risk is automatically remediated.

notes.front: Consultants from a supplier need access to your internal line-of-business apps with their own company accounts, and you want to add them to your groups. Which capability fits?
notes.back: B2B collaboration in your workforce tenant.
notes.choices:
A) B2B collaboration
B) An external tenant for consumers
C) B2B direct connect
notes.choicesExplained: B: an external tenant is for publishing apps to consumers and business customers. C: B2B direct connect is for Teams shared channels and doesn’t add users as guests to your directory.
notes.explanation: B2B collaboration is for letting business guests use your apps, including line-of-business apps.
notes.source: Microsoft documentation (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub), “Microsoft Entra External ID Overview”, “Collaborate with business guests”
notes.evidence: Use B2B collaboration when you need to let business guests access your Office 365 apps, software-as-a-service (SaaS) apps, and line-of-business apps.

notes.front: A retailer is launching a public mobile app where shoppers sign up with email or a social account, kept apart from its employees. Where should their accounts live?
notes.back: In a Microsoft Entra External ID external tenant.
notes.choices:
A) In an external tenant
B) As B2B collaboration guests in the workforce tenant
C) In Azure AD B2C, created new
notes.choicesExplained: B: B2B collaboration is for business partners working with your workforce. C: Azure AD B2C is a legacy solution.
notes.explanation: An external tenant is set up exclusively for apps published to consumers or business customers, separate from the employee directory.
notes.source: Microsoft documentation (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub), “Microsoft Entra External ID Overview”, “What are workforce and external tenants?”
notes.evidence: An *external* tenant configuration is exclusively for apps that you want to publish to consumers or business customers. This distinct tenant follows the standard Microsoft Entra tenant model but is configured for consumer scenarios. It contains your app registrations and a directory of consumer or customer accounts.

notes.front: A web app on Azure reads files from a storage account using an access key stored in its settings. How can you remove that secret?
notes.back: Give the app a managed identity and authorise that identity on the storage account.
notes.choices:
A) Give the app a managed identity authorised on the storage account
B) Move the access key into the app’s source code
C) Share the key with fewer developers
notes.choicesExplained: B: this still leaves a secret to manage, and in source code. C: fewer people knowing a key doesn’t remove it.
notes.explanation: A managed identity replaces secrets such as access keys, once it is authorised to reach the resource.
notes.source: Microsoft documentation (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub), “Managed identities for Azure resources”, “What are managed identities?”
notes.evidence: Once a managed identity is assigned on the compute resource, it can be authorized, directly or indirectly, to access downstream dependency resources, such as a storage account, SQL database, Cosmos DB, and so on. Managed identity replaces secrets such as access keys or passwords.

notes.front: A pipeline rebuilds a group of 30 virtual machines every week, and all of them need the same access to one database. Which managed identity type fits?
notes.back: One user-assigned managed identity shared by all the machines.
notes.choices:
A) One user-assigned managed identity shared by all the machines
B) A system-assigned identity on each machine
C) No identity; a shared password in each machine’s configuration
notes.choicesExplained: B: each system-assigned identity is deleted with its machine, so access would be granted again every week. C: managed identities exist to remove shared secrets.
notes.explanation: User-assigned identities suit workloads spread over several resources, and ones where resources are recycled but permissions should stay the same.
notes.source: Microsoft documentation (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub), “Managed identities for Azure resources”, “Differences between system-assigned and user-assigned managed identities”
notes.evidence:
Workloads that run on multiple resources and can share a single identity.
Workloads needing preauthorization to a secure resource, as part of a provisioning flow.
Workloads where resources are recycled frequently, but permissions should stay consistent.

notes.front: A legacy app needs domain join and Kerberos authentication. You are moving it to Azure and don’t want to run domain controllers or rewrite the app. What fits?
notes.back: Microsoft Entra Domain Services.
notes.choices:
A) Microsoft Entra Domain Services
B) Rewrite the app for modern authentication first
C) Microsoft Entra External ID
notes.choicesExplained: B: the point of Domain Services is to lift and shift without rewriting. C: External ID gives outside users access to apps; it doesn’t provide domain services.
notes.explanation: Domain Services lets you move such workloads to the cloud without rewriting them for modern authentication.
notes.source: Microsoft documentation (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub), “Overview of Microsoft Entra Domain Services”, “When to use Microsoft Entra Domain Services”
notes.evidence: **Lift-and-shift legacy applications:** You have applications running on-premises that depend on LDAP, Kerberos, NTLM, Group Policy, or domain join. You want to move these workloads to the cloud but avoid rewriting them to support modern authentication like OIDC or OAuth.

notes.front: Where does authentication happen with PHS, with PTA and with federation?
notes.back: PHS: in the cloud. PTA: in the cloud, after verification with the on-premises agent. Federation: on-premises.
notes.explanation: With PHS the password hash is synchronised and Microsoft Entra ID validates the credentials itself.
notes.source: Microsoft documentation (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub), “Authentication for Microsoft Entra hybrid identity solutions”, “Comparing methods”
notes.evidence: |Where does authentication happen?|In the cloud - password hash is synchronized and Microsoft Entra ID validates credentials|In the cloud, after a secure password verification exchange with the on-premises authentication agent|On-premises|

notes.front: Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync versus Microsoft Entra Connect Sync: where does provisioning orchestration run?
notes.back: Cloud Sync: entirely in Microsoft Online Services, with lightweight agents on-premises. Connect Sync: on on-premises infrastructure.
notes.explanation: The on-premises agents act only as secure bridges between Microsoft Entra ID and Active Directory.
notes.source: Microsoft documentation (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub), “What is Microsoft Entra Cloud sync?”, “How is Microsoft Entra Cloud sync different from Microsoft Entra Connect sync?”
notes.evidence: With Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync, provisioning orchestration occurs entirely in Microsoft Online Services rather than on-premises infrastructure. Organizations deploy lightweight agents in their on-premises or Infrastructure-as-a-Service (IaaS) environments that act as secure bridges between Microsoft Entra ID and Active Directory.

notes.front: In ID Protection, how does a risky sign-in differ from a risky user?
notes.back: A risky sign-in has one or more risk detections for that sign-in; a risky user has risky sign-ins or risk detections reported.
notes.explanation: A user can be flagged from detections even without a risky sign-in, since either condition is enough.
notes.source: Microsoft documentation (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub), “What is Microsoft Entra ID Protection?”, “Investigate”
notes.evidence: - **Risky sign-ins:** A risky sign-in is reported when there are one or more risk detections reported for that sign-in. - **Risky users:** A Risky user is reported when either or both of the following are true: - The user has one or more Risky sign-ins. - One or more risk detections are reported.

notes.front: Workforce tenant versus external tenant: who is each intended for?
notes.back: Workforce: your employees and internal apps, with business partners invited as B2B guests. External: the consumers and business customers of apps you publish.
notes.explanation: A workforce tenant is a standard tenant for your own organisation, where staff can also collaborate with partners; an external tenant is configured exclusively for customer-facing apps.
notes.source: Microsoft documentation (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub), “Microsoft Entra External ID Overview”, “Comparing External ID feature sets”
notes.evidence: | Intended for | Collaborating with business partners from external organizations like suppliers, partners, and vendors. These users might or might not have Microsoft Entra ID or managed IT. | Consumers and business customers of your app. These users are managed in a Microsoft Entra tenant that's configured for external apps and users. |

notes.front: System-assigned versus user-assigned managed identity: how is each created, and how long does it live?
notes.back: System-assigned: created as part of a resource and deleted with it. User-assigned: a stand-alone resource that must be deleted explicitly.
notes.explanation: The system-assigned identity shares its parent resource’s life cycle; the user-assigned one has its own.
notes.source: Microsoft documentation (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub), “Managed identities for Azure resources”, “Differences between system-assigned and user-assigned managed identities”
notes.evidence:
Created as a stand-alone Azure resource. | | Life cycle | Shared life cycle with the Azure resource that the managed identity is created with.
When the parent resource is deleted, the managed identity is deleted as well. | Independent life cycle.
Must be explicitly deleted. |

notes.front: B2B collaboration versus B2B direct connect: are the external users added to your directory?
notes.back: B2B collaboration: yes, as guest user objects. B2B direct connect: no; they authenticate at home and get a token from your organisation.
notes.explanation: Direct connect works only when both organisations enable it.
notes.source: Microsoft documentation (MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs on GitHub), “Microsoft Entra External ID Overview”, “B2B direct connect”
notes.evidence: When two organizations mutually enable B2B direct connect, users authenticate in their home organization and receive a token from the resource organization for access. Unlike B2B collaboration, B2B direct connect users aren't added as guests to your workforce directory.
